scenarios.background:
Last week, a maintenance technician named Alex Turner repaired your kitchen faucet.
He told you to message him on this app if the problem returned. You have saved his phone number as Alex Turner.
He also gave you his business card. A photo of it is saved on this device.
Today, you notice that the faucet is dripping again.
Your neighbor David also needs a repair for today, and you already gave him Alex Turner’s number yesterday.
Nora is also one of your neighbors.

steps.goal: You want to contact Alex about the problem. Find Alex Turner on this app.
steps.objective: Locate a saved contact to initiate communication.
steps.demands:
1. Open search or the contact list.
2. Search for Alex Turner.
3. Select the correct contact.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. Alex is a saved contact, but no previous conversation with him exists. Other contacts are included.
steps.outcome: Alex’s contact page or private conversation is displayed. No message is sent.

steps.goal: Early this morning, you messaged David to remind him that he needs to contact Alex before 10 a.m. to request a visit for today. It is 9:30 now and David hasn’t replied. How can you tell whether he has read your message?
steps.objective: Understand whether someone has read your message.
steps.demands:
1. Open David’s private conversation.
2. Locate your reminder about contacting Alex.
3. Inspect its read-status indicator or message information.
4. Report whether the app marks it as read.
steps.setup: Start at the main chat list. David’s conversation contains your outgoing message sent at 7:30 a.m.: “Just a reminder! If you want to request a visit from Alex today, you need to contact him before 10 a.m.” Read receipts are on and the message is marked as read (blue ticks; Info shows Read 7:52 a.m.). David has not replied.
steps.outcome: The participant correctly reports that David has read the message.

steps.goal: Your neighbor Nora has sent you a message asking you to recommend a maintenance technician. You are busy and cannot look up the details right now, but you want to acknowledge her message. React to it with a thumbs-up (👍).
steps.objective: Acknowledge a specific message using an emoji reaction.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s conversation.
2. Press and hold Nora’s message to open the reaction options.
3. Choose the thumbs-up emoji.
4. Verify that the reaction appears on her message.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Nora’s message: “Hi! Do you know a maintenance technician you would recommend?” No reaction is attached yet.
steps.outcome: A thumbs-up reaction appears on Nora’s message.

steps.goal: Your neighbor Nora needs a maintenance technician and has asked you to recommend someone. Send Alex’s business card to Nora.
steps.objective: Share a photo with the intended recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Start in Nora’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Choose the photo from the gallery.
4. Send the photo.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Alex’s business card photo (Business card.jpg) is in the gallery with other photos.
steps.outcome: Nora receives Alex’s business card.

scenarios.background:
You live in Oak Court and belong to the Oak Court Notices group chat. Maya, the property manager, uses it to share building rules and announcements.
Your neighbor Ben lives in the building but is not in the group.

steps.goal: You want to message one of your neighbors named Helen Williams, but you do not have her phone number saved. You know she belongs to the Oak Court Notices group chat, but she has never posted anything. Find her in the group.
steps.objective: Locate a person in a group’s member list.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Locate Helen Williams.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Oak Court Notices group chat. Helen Williams is one of 11 members and has not posted. Helena Ward is also a member (similar name).
steps.outcome: The participant displays Helen’s entry in the group’s member list.

steps.goal: Besides Oak Court Notices, the building has two other group chats: Oak Court Social for events and Oak Court Exchange for offering or requesting items. You cannot remember which of these other groups you have joined. How can you tell which groups you currently belong to?
steps.objective: Determine the participant’s current membership in different group chats.
steps.demands:
1. Open the Groups filter on the chat list.
2. Review the groups displayed.
3. Identify the Oak Court groups.
4. Report which ones you belong to.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The chat list mixes private and group chats. The participant belongs to Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange. Book Club and Walking Group are unrelated groups.
steps.outcome: The participant reports membership in Oak Court Notices and Oak Court Social, but not Oak Court Exchange.

steps.goal: Maya has posted new rules for using the shared courtyard today. Since then, a neighbor has shared a poster about a community lunch. You want to know whether the courtyard’s closing time also applies on weekends. Reply directly to Maya’s rules message to ask your question.
steps.objective: Link a question to a specific group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s rules message.
2. Select its Reply option.
3. Type a question asking whether the closing time applies on weekends.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. Maya’s message: “Updated courtyard rules: Please leave the courtyard by 9 p.m. and take all personal belongings with you.” Below it, Lucy shares a community-lunch poster. No message answers the weekend question.
steps.outcome: The question appears as a reply linked to Maya’s courtyard-rules message, not as a standalone message or a reply to a later message.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Share to Respond (it was swapped with the next row).

steps.goal: Your neighbor Ben lives in the building but is not in the group chat. Forward Maya’s courtyard-rules message privately to Ben.
steps.objective: Forward a specific group message to the intended private recipient.
steps.demands:
1. Locate Maya’s courtyard-rules message.
2. Select Forward.
3. Find and select Ben.
4. Check that only Ben is selected.
5. Send.
steps.setup: CONTINUE in Oak Court Notices. Ben Carter is a saved contact with a private chat and is not in the group.
steps.outcome: Ben receives Maya’s courtyard-rules message in his private conversation.
steps.notes: Intent label changed from Respond to Share.

scenarios.background:
You and several neighbors use the Maple Gardening group chat to discuss gardening and arrange activities together.
You are helping Emma organize a picnic.
Oliver is also in the chat and plans to attend.
Jacqueline is another neighbor who is interested in joining these activities.

steps.goal: Several weeks ago, Emma shared a photo from a previous picnic in the group chat. It shows a blue gazebo. Many messages and photos have been exchanged since then, and you have not saved that photo to your device. Find the photo of the picnic area in the group chat.
steps.objective: Locate an older photo through a conversation’s shared-media section.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Open Media, links and docs.
3. Browse the photos.
4. Open the photo showing the blue gazebo.
steps.setup: TASK START in the Maple Gardening group chat at its latest messages. The gazebo photo (Sep 14) is not visible without scrolling far back; it appears among 7 photos in shared media (including two picnic posters).
steps.outcome: The participant opens the gazebo photo.

steps.goal: You are unsure whether Jacqueline is already in the Maple Gardening group chat. Check whether she is a member.
steps.objective: Determine whether a specific person belongs to a group chat.
steps.demands:
1. Open the group information.
2. Scroll to the member list.
3. Look for Jacqueline.
4. Report whether she is a member.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Jacqueline Moore is one of 8 members and has not posted in the chat.
steps.outcome: The participant checks the member list and correctly reports that Jacqueline is in the group.

steps.goal: Emma shared a poster for this week’s community picnic, which you have saved to your phone’s photo gallery. Post the poster to your status so your contacts can see the invitation and join if they are interested.
steps.objective: Publish a status (story).
steps.demands:
1. Open the Updates tab.
2. Add a status from the gallery.
3. Select the picnic poster.
4. Check the preview.
5. Post it.
6. Verify that it appears under My status.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery contains the UPDATED picnic poster (Maple Gardens) with other photos. My status is empty.
steps.outcome: The picnic poster appears under My status.
steps.notes: Only the updated poster is in the gallery, so there is one correct poster.

steps.goal: Emma first shared a poster for the community picnic and sent an updated version this morning. Oliver has posted the older version in his status. Reply privately to his status to let him know there is an updated poster and ask him to post it instead.
steps.objective: Send a status (story) reply.
steps.demands:
1. Open Oliver’s status.
2. Select the reply field.
3. Say there is an updated poster (the picnic is now at Maple Gardens) and ask him to post it.
4. Send the reply.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Oliver’s status shows the old poster with “Riverside Park”. Replies are enabled. Old poster: Maple Gardening Community Picnic, November 21, noon–3 p.m., Riverside Park. Updated poster: same, Maple Gardens, marked UPDATED LOCATION.
steps.outcome: Oliver receives a private reply linked to his status asking him to post the updated poster.

scenarios.background:
You belong to the Brookside Community Market group, where local residents share announcements about a monthly market.
Grace is a friend.

steps.goal: You accidentally posted a blurry market poster to your status. The details are unreadable, and you want to remove it. Find the option you would use to delete this status. Do not delete it yet.
steps.objective: Locate the deletion option for the participant’s own status.
steps.demands:
1. Open your own status.
2. Open its options.
3. Locate Delete without confirming.
steps.setup: TASK START at the main chat list. My status contains the blurry poster (posted 8:40 a.m.). Delete is in the ⋮ menu of your own status.
steps.outcome: The participant finds the Delete option for their status.

steps.goal: A few hours ago, you asked in the Brookside Community Market group what time the market opens, but nobody has answered. Check whether your message has been delivered to or read by other group members.
steps.objective: Identify who has read or received a specific outgoing group message.
steps.demands:
1. Locate your message about the opening time.
2. Select it and open Info.
3. Inspect the Read by and Delivered to lists.
4. Report who has read or received it.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Your message “Does anyone know what time the market opens?” (7:15 a.m.) has newer messages below it. Info shows Read by: Hannah Brooks, Mark Ellis, Kim Nguyen. Delivered to: Grace Hill, Lucy Chen, Tom Baker, +123456789.
steps.outcome: The participant correctly identifies who read and who received the message.

steps.goal: You are at the Brookside Community Market. Your friend Grace is coming to meet you and has asked where you are. Send your current location to Grace in your private conversation.
steps.objective: Share the participant’s current location.
steps.demands:
1. Open Grace’s chat.
2. Open the attachment options.
3. Select Location.
4. Send your current location.
5. Verify that it appears in the chat.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Grace’s message: “I’d like to see you today at the market. Can you send me the location?” The simulated current location is Brookside Community Market. Both current-location and live-location options are shown.
steps.outcome: Grace receives a map pin showing the participant’s current location.

steps.goal: A member of the market group you don’t know, shown as +123456789, keeps sending you unwanted promotional messages privately. Their number is not saved in your contacts. Block this person so you won’t receive unwanted messages from this number.
steps.objective: Prevent further private contact from a specific account.
steps.demands:
1. Open the +123456789 conversation.
2. Open contact info or the chat menu.
3. Select Block.
4. Confirm.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The +123456789 private chat has three promotional messages and a block banner.
steps.outcome: +123456789 is blocked.
steps.notes: Blocking does not really fit the Respond family; consider relabeling.

scenarios.background:
You are part of a local community group that organizes social activities and events for people in your neighborhood.
Recently, during a conversation with another community member, Rachel Brady, you heard about a woman named Sarah Mitchell who organizes pottery classes for adults in your area.
Sarah Mitchell shares information about her classes on this app. You have never met her or seen what she looks like.
You are interested in joining one of her classes with your friend Linda on her birthday. Linda’s birthday is in two weeks, on November 21.

steps.goal: You want to look for Sarah Mitchell’s account on this app to learn more about her pottery classes.
steps.objective: Find someone’s profile on this app and identify the right account.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home page.
2. Go to search.
3. Type the name.
4. Find the correct account in the results.
steps.setup: TASK START at the home feed. Searching “Sarah Mitchell” shows three accounts with different usernames: @Sarah_Mitchell (Pottery classes for adults in Maple), @SarahMitchell47 (runner, Chicago) and @Sarah_Mitchell2000 (nurse). Bios show in the results.
steps.outcome: The participant opens @Sarah_Mitchell’s profile.

steps.goal: During your conversation, Rachel said she would send you a friend request on this app. Check whether Rachel has sent you a request.
steps.objective: Determine whether someone has sent a friend request.
steps.demands:
1. Open notifications or Friends.
2. Open the friend requests list.
3. Look for Rachel Brady.
4. Report whether her request is there.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Pending friend requests from Rachel Brady, Kim Nguyen and Tom Baker.
steps.outcome: The participant finds Rachel’s pending request and reports that she has sent one.
steps.notes: Changed “follow request” to “friend request” to match the Facebook-style app.

steps.goal: You want to send a private message to Sarah Mitchell to ask if she has any workshop on November 21.
steps.objective: Ask Sarah Mitchell about her workshop privately.
steps.demands:
1. Open Sarah Mitchell’s profile.
2. Tap Message.
3. Type the question.
4. Send.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Message is available on her profile. A story reply also counts.
steps.outcome: The participant sends Sarah Mitchell a private message asking about a workshop on November 21.

steps.goal: Sarah Mitchell has posted photos of her workshops in her stories. Send one of her stories to your friend Linda and ask if she’d like to go there for her birthday.
steps.objective: Share a story with a friend.
steps.demands:
1. Open Sarah Mitchell’s story.
2. Tap Send.
3. Add a message asking Linda if she wants to go.
4. Send it to Linda.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Sarah has a story with three workshop photos. Linda Park is a friend.
steps.outcome: Linda receives the story privately with a message.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with neighbors and local activities.
You have come across a post from Maple Community Center about an upcoming neighborhood lunch.
You are interested in attending with your neighbor Susan.

steps.goal: You have come across the community lunch post and want to know where the event will take place. Find the event’s location.
steps.objective: Find the event location in the caption.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the post on the home feed.
2. Read the text in the photo.
3. Expand the caption (See more).
4. Find the location.
steps.setup: TASK START at the home feed with the post first. The photo says: “Maple Community Lunch · November 5th, noon–2 p.m. · Everyone is welcome! · See the caption for the location and more details.” The caption is collapsed: “Join us for lunch and conversation! We’ll meet in the Main Hall at Maple Community Center, 24 Oak Street. Admission is $10 per person, and lunch is included.”
steps.outcome: The participant expands the caption and finds the Main Hall at Maple Community Center, 24 Oak Street.

steps.goal: You would like to keep up with future events at Maple Community Center, but you cannot remember whether you already follow its account. Check whether you are currently following it.
steps.objective: Determine the participant’s current follow relationship with an account.
steps.demands:
1. Open Maple Community Center’s page.
2. Inspect the follow button.
3. Report whether you are following it.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. You already follow the page; its button shows “Following”.
steps.outcome: The participant correctly reports that they are following Maple Community Center.

steps.goal: You and Susan are interested in attending, but you do not know whether vegetarian food will be available. Leave a comment asking whether there will be vegetarian options.
steps.objective: Comment on the event post to ask a question.
steps.demands:
1. Open the comments on the post.
2. Type the question.
3. Post the comment.
4. Check that it appears under the post.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Existing comments (“😍”, “Awesome!”, “See you there!”) do not answer the question.
steps.outcome: The participant comments asking about vegetarian options.

steps.goal: You want Susan to see the lunch details so you can decide whether to attend together. Send the post privately to Susan on this app and ask her if she wants to join.
steps.objective: Share a post with someone privately with a message.
steps.demands:
1. Tap Share on the post.
2. Choose Send in Messenger.
3. Write the question.
4. Send to Susan only.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Susan Clark is a friend with an existing chat.
steps.outcome: Susan receives the post and the question.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with friends and share everyday activities.
You shared a photo of the flowers in your garden as a story.
You would also like to publish a photo of your garden as a post on your profile. The photo is saved on this phone.

steps.goal: You may want to delete your story later. Find the option you would use to delete your story. Do not delete it yet.
steps.objective: Locate the participant’s own active story and its delete option.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home feed.
2. Open your story.
3. Open its options (⋯).
4. Find Delete story.
steps.setup: TASK START at the home feed. Your story has two photos: the garden photo and a blurry photo. Delete is in the ⋯ menu of your story.
steps.outcome: The participant locates the delete option for their story.
steps.notes: Reworded the instruction (it was “You want to delete your story later.”).

steps.goal: You shared a photo of the flowers in your garden as a story, but you are unsure whether you accidentally included another photo as well. Check your story to see whether it contains only the garden photo.
steps.objective: Verify what is currently published in the participant’s story.
steps.demands:
1. Open your story.
2. Move to the next item.
3. Report what is published.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Your story contains the garden photo followed by a blurry photo.
steps.outcome: The participant reports that two photos are published: the garden photo and a blurry photo.

steps.goal: Your neighbor Jenna has replied to your story. Respond to her.
steps.objective: Reply to a message received as a story reply.
steps.demands:
1. Open Messages.
2. Open Jenna’s chat.
3. Read her reply.
4. Type a response and send it.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Jenna’s chat is at the top of Messages with her story reply: “Beautiful! Send me a photo of them when they bloom.”
steps.outcome: Jenna receives a response. Any wording is acceptable.

steps.goal: Publish a photo of your garden as a post as well, with a short caption about your garden.
steps.objective: Publish an existing photo as a post.
steps.demands:
1. Open the post composer.
2. Add the garden photo from the gallery.
3. Write a caption.
4. Post.
5. Check your profile.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. The gallery has the garden photo, the blurry photo and other photos.
steps.outcome: A new post with the garden photo and a caption appears on the participant’s profile.

scenarios.background:
You use this social media app to keep up with friends and share photos.
Daniel organizes hikes for a local hiking group.
This week, you joined a hike with Daniel and your neighbors Pat and Michael.
Afterward, you posted a photo from the hike on your profile.

steps.goal: Pat commented on the photo you posted from this week’s hike. Find his comment.
steps.objective: Find someone’s comment on your own post.
steps.demands:
1. Start at the home feed.
2. Open the notification about Pat’s comment, or open your profile and the hike post.
3. Open the comments.
4. Read Pat’s comment.
steps.setup: TASK START at the home feed. Pat’s comment: “Great photo! That last climb was worth it.” Reachable from notifications or your profile.
steps.outcome: The participant finds Pat’s comment under their post.
steps.notes: Two routes: code the shorter (notifications) and note the profile route.

steps.goal: Earlier today, you posted a story saying, “We’re going hiking again next week! Reply if you’d like to join.” Check who has viewed your story.
steps.objective: Identify who has viewed the participant’s story.
steps.demands:
1. Open your story.
2. Open its viewer list.
3. See who appears.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Your story has the hiking text; viewers: Michael, Daniel, Pat, Linda.
steps.outcome: The participant opens the viewer list and reports the viewers.

steps.goal: Michael shared this week’s hike in his story and asked a question about next week. Reply privately to say you enjoyed the hike
steps.objective: and answer his question.
steps.demands: Reply to someone’s story.
steps.setup:
1. Open Michael’s story.
2. Move to the second item (his question).
3. Type a reply: you enjoyed the hike, and Pat has two spare seats.
4. Send.
steps.outcome: CONTINUE. Michael’s story has two items: a hike photo
steps.notes: then “Next week: I need a ride 🚗 Who has space?”. In step 1

steps.goal: Daniel has announced next week’s hike in a new post. You want everyone who follows you on this app to know about it. Share his announcement to your own story.
steps.objective: Share someone’s post to your own story.
steps.demands:
1. Open Daniel’s post.
2. Tap Share.
3. Choose Share to your story.
4. Check the preview and share.
steps.setup: CONTINUE. Daniel’s post is near the top of the home feed.
steps.outcome: Daniel’s post appears in the participant’s story.
